newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Main Latam bank stocks outpacing fundamentals - ING.
newsitem.headline: Main Latam bank stocks outpacing fundamentals - ING.

text.p: Banking shares in Brazil and Mexico appear to be outpacing fundamentals in Latin America's two biggest markets, Dutch investment bank ING Barings said.
"A recent visit to Brazil has once more reinforced our cautious growth scenario," said the report titled "Are prices shooting over fundamentals in our two largest markets?"

It also said fourth-quarter asset quality figures for Mexican banks were "worse than our already depressed expectations and have taken away hopes for the large banks in the system at least for the short-term."
ING said poor asset quality and a high ratio of past-due loans to total loans within the Mexican financial system "are dangerous" and recommended selectivity over the long term.
"We would be buyers of smaller quality banks that can grow their way out of problems, such as GF Banorte," it said. "(But), we remain cautious on larger banks."
In Brazil, it said, "lending remains tricky, and banks are making vigorous effort to find new sources of revenue. For now, insurance is expected to be the savior."
ING said Brazilian banking shares have risen too quickly "owing to growth expectations that have not been realized" and it sees "no significant upside."
It said it maintains its underweight position on the Brazilian banking sector and its holding rating on the three largest private banks Unibanco, Itau and Bradesco.

"Despite our belief that the Brazilian economy presents significant opportunities in the future, we believe the valuation multiples ... have run ahead of modest growth expectations for the 1997-98 period," the report said.
Peru remained its favorite market "with significant values still available" as largest Peruvian banks Credicorp and Wiese continue to trade under their fair value, ING said.

Market expectations for large Chilean banks are too high but profitable niche players still trade at a discount and, in Colombia, Banco de Colombia continues to trade "at an extremely attractive valuation," it said.
Argentine bank shares remain "comfortable" over the long term as growth remains strong but, in the short term, they will continue to suffer from market corrections, it said.
